prompt: A prospect writes: "We have a working web app but it is slow and the original freelancer has gone. Can you help?" Which agency service fits this request first?

options: A code audit followed by ongoing maintenance and performance work
A brand-new MVP build from scratch
A UI/UX redesign of the marketing site
A white-label app licence
mcq.explanation: They already have a product; the risk is unknown code quality. An audit tells you what you are inheriting, and a maintenance or improvement retainer is the natural follow-on. Rebuilding from scratch is a later decision, not the first offer.

prompt: Which description best separates a fixed-price project from a dedicated team (staff augmentation) engagement?

options: Fixed price sells a defined scope for an agreed sum; a dedicated team sells engineers' time each month and the client directs the work
Fixed price is always cheaper for the client than a dedicated team
A dedicated team always includes a project manager and QA, fixed price never does
Fixed price is only used for mobile apps, dedicated teams only for web
mcq.explanation: The difference is what is being bought: an outcome against a scope, or capacity over time. Cost, staffing and platform vary case by case.

prompt: A founder asks for "an Uber-like app" with a firm launch date in 10 weeks, a fixed budget and a scope that is still changing weekly. Which engagement model do you recommend?

options: Fixed price for the whole idea as described today
Hourly with no estimate, since the scope keeps changing
A dedicated team of six engineers from day one
A short paid discovery phase to fix the MVP scope, then fixed price for that phase
mcq.explanation: A moving scope makes a fixed price for everything a loss or a fight later, and open-ended hourly with a fixed budget worries the founder. Paid discovery turns the moving idea into a scope you can price honestly.

prompt: An existing client's app has launched. Which follow-on offer usually creates recurring revenue for an agency while genuinely helping the client?

options: A second, separate discovery phase for the same app
A one-off logo redesign
Reselling them the same app under a new name
A monthly maintenance and support retainer covering fixes, OS/library updates and small improvements
mcq.explanation: Launched software needs updates, monitoring and fixes; a retainer prices that predictable need and keeps the relationship alive for the next phase.

prompt: A client wants to go from idea to a launched mobile app. Put the agency services in the order they would normally be delivered.

task.prompt: A client wants to go from idea to a launched mobile app. Put the agency services in the order they would normally be delivered.
task.explanation: Scope first, then design what you scoped, build it, test it, ship it, and keep it running. Selling maintenance before launch is fine, but delivery follows this order.

prompt: An inbound lead, a regional gym chain, writes: "We want members to book classes and pay from their phones. We have a website on WordPress. Budget not decided."

task.prompt: An inbound lead, a regional gym chain, writes: "We want members to book classes and pay from their phones. We have a website on WordPress. Budget not decided."

steps.question: Which service line is the core of this request?
options: Staff augmentation of one QA engineer
Mobile app development with booking and payments
SEO for the WordPress site
Data analytics dashboards
steps.explanation: Booking and paying from phones is a mobile product with payments; the website is context.

steps.question: They mention their WordPress site often breaks. What do you do with that?
options: Ignore it, it is not what they asked for
Lead with a full website rebuild instead of the app
Note it as a possible second service (maintenance or a rebuild) and raise it after the main need is scoped
steps.explanation: It is a real cross-sell, but leading with it derails the call from the need they came with.

steps.question: Budget is undecided. What is the best next step?
options: Offer a short discovery call, then a ballpark range for an MVP so they can anchor a budget
Send a fixed quote for the full app today
Wait until they tell you a budget
steps.explanation: Buyers rarely know a budget for something new; a range after discovery gives them something real to plan with.

prompt: This is a draft "Services" paragraph a new BD hire wrote for a capabilities one-pager. Mark the sentences that are problems.

task.prompt: This is a draft "Services" paragraph a new BD hire wrote for a capabilities one-pager. Mark the sentences that are problems.

segments.text: We design, build and maintain web and mobile apps for startups and growing businesses.
We can build absolutely anything in any technology within any budget.
segments.issue: Overpromises; no agency can, and buyers stop trusting the rest of the page.

segments.text: Typical engagements run as fixed-price projects or monthly dedicated teams.
We add AI features such as chat assistants and document search where they solve a real problem.
Our apps never have bugs, so you will not need support after launch.
segments.issue: False claim, and it talks the client out of a maintenance retainer.

segments.text: After launch we offer maintenance plans covering updates, fixes and small improvements.

prompt: A prospect sends five requests. Rank them by how well each fits a typical web/mobile/AI product agency, best fit first.

task.prompt: A prospect sends five requests. Rank them by how well each fits a typical web/mobile/AI product agency, best fit first.

items.label: Take over maintenance of their existing React Native app
Run their paid social media ads
Build an MVP of a marketplace web app with payments
Add an AI support chatbot to their existing SaaS product

task.explanation: Product builds, AI features and app maintenance are core software services. Paid ads are a marketing agency's work and hardware is not a software service at all; refer those out.

prompt: A client asks for a rough comparison of two engagement models for a 3-month build. Calculate both totals.

task.prompt: A client asks for a rough comparison of two engagement models for a 3-month build. Calculate both totals.

rows: Scope estimated at 960 hours at $40/hour, plus a 15% risk buffer
2 developers at $4,800/month each + 1 part-time QA at $2,000/month, for 3 months

task.explanation: Fixed: 960 x 40 = 38,400; x 1.15 = 44,160. Team: (2 x 4,800 + 2,000) x 3 = 34,800. The difference is the client paying the agency to carry scope risk.

prompt: An existing client, a logistics startup, has a web app you built last year. Their CTO emails: "Can you lend us two React developers for six months? We will manage them."

task.prompt: An existing client, a logistics startup, has a web app you built last year. Their CTO emails: "Can you lend us two React developers for six months? We will manage them."

steps.question: Which engagement model is this?
options: Discovery workshop
Staff augmentation / dedicated team
Fixed-price project
White-label licence
steps.explanation: They direct the work and buy capacity over time.

steps.question: What should you clarify before quoting?
options: Their full feature list and a signed SOW
Which logo they want on the app
Seniority needed, overlap hours/time zone, start date, and how tasks and reviews will be run
steps.explanation: For augmentation the scope is the people and the working arrangement, not a feature list.

steps.question: Halfway through they ask the two developers to also design the new UI. What do you do?
options: Flag that design is a different role and offer a designer for agreed hours
Tell the developers to do the design quietly
Refuse and end the engagement
steps.explanation: In augmentation the scope is the roles bought; adding a role is a change you price, not a favour you absorb.

prompt: A BD rep's notes describing the agency's services for a prospect call. Mark the statements that would mislead the prospect.

task.prompt: A BD rep's notes describing the agency's services for a prospect call. Mark the statements that would mislead the prospect.

segments.text: Discovery is a short paid phase that produces a scope, wireframes and an estimate.
Fixed price means the client can add features at any time without changing the price.
segments.issue: Fixed price covers the agreed scope; additions go through change requests.

segments.text: A dedicated team bills monthly for the people assigned, and the client sets priorities.
Maintenance retainers include unlimited new features every month.
segments.issue: Retainers usually cover fixes, updates and a set number of hours, not unlimited new development.

segments.text: QA runs throughout development, not only at the end.
Launch includes help with app store submission.
